Thanks. A few legal guardrails:

1) Avoid absolute statements about data residency for the hosted API. We can say: "Requests sent to our Hosted API may be processed in the region you choose when available; depending on capacity and routing, processing may occur in other regions. We use contractual and technical safeguards for cross-border transfers (see DPA)."

2) Subprocessor listing: preferable to list categories + top-level vendor names and primary function rather than an exhaustive running list in a public slide. For procurement packets we'll provide the full spreadsheet under NDA, but the public-friendly summary should be short.

3) Don't promise specific certifications unless they are current and reflected in our compliance docs. Reference the SOC 2 report and DPA link.

I've attached a marked-up plain-language DPA draft (dpa_plainlang_draft.md) with suggested wording and a short disclaimer. Please incorporate the suggestions into the public snippet.

-Kim

--- draft public snippet (for product console & one-pager) ---
Redwood Inference processes customer API requests in the region selected by the customer when available. To support inference, we rely on a small set of trusted subprocessors for cloud infrastructure, logging, and monitoring. We publish a summary of those subprocessors and the safeguards we use; you can request the full list under NDA. Our DPA describes cross-border transfers and legal safeguards, and our SOC 2 report is available on request.

Key subprocessors (public summary):
- Cloud provider — compute and storage (primary region-based deployments)
- Log storage & analytics — audit and usage telemetry
- Monitoring & alerting — service health and incident response
- Key management — encryption key custody partner
- CDN & networking — edge routing and caching
- Billing & metrics — invoicing and usage aggregation

--- end snippet ---
